mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, which reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 8.5% over a 3-month window signals improving labor market conditions, which increases consumer confidence and corporate hiring, leading to higher expected earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE < 8.5% (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal fails to outperform baseline in 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both residential construction permits (HOUST) and personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong underlying demand growth, which signals rising corporate revenues and positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances, or the interaction term's Rank IC is below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates strengthening supply-side capacity, which reduces input cost pressures and improves profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month MA (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal generates negative returns in more than 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening demand environment, which triggers risk-off behavior and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 1.5% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS declines and UNRATE rises, or the interaction signal fails to achieve Rank IC > 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% year-over-year, combined with a stable or rising federal funds rate, indicates inflationary pressures that prompt the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of CPI > 3.0% YoY and FEDFUNDS >= 0.07%, or the interaction signal's Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k per month, combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS > 200k and UNRATE < 9.0%, or the interaction term fails to achieve Rank IC > 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters, combined with a decline in residential construction (HOUST), indicates a deepening demand slowdown that triggers equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines > 0.5% QoQ for 2 consecutive quarters and HOUST < 650k
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDP contractions and HOUST < 650k, or the interaction signal's Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year window.
